kangaroo-ca-2017-g0910-01.title: Fill in from the right
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0910-01.body:
- Bottom middle: $2020 - 2017 = 3$.
- Middle left: $2039 - 2020 = 19$.
- The middle-left cell is the sum of "?" and the bottom middle cell: $? = 19 - 3 = 16$.

**Answer: (B) 16**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0910-02.title: Pages per minute
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0910-02.body:
$24 : 1.5 = 16$ pages per minute, so in 5 minutes it prints $16 \cdot 5 = 80$ pages.

**Answer: (C) 80**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0910-02.title: Scale the time
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0910-02.body:
In 3 minutes it prints 48 pages, in half a minute 8 pages. So in $5 = 3 + 3 - 1$ minutes: $48 + 48 - 16 = 80$ pages.

**Answer: (C) 80**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0910-06.title: Go around the circle
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0910-06.body:
Going left from Bianca, Antonia is 5 steps away; going right, 8 steps. Walking all the way around the circle (left from Bianca to Antonia, then on to Bianca the other way) takes $5 + 8 = 13$ steps, one step per girl. So there are 13 girls.

Check: between them there are 4 girls on one side and 7 on the other: $4 + 7 + 2 = 13$.

**Answer: (C) 13**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0910-12.title: Divisible by 5 and by 3
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0910-12.body:
The product is always positive. 

**By 5:** $\overline{7b8}$ ends in 8, so it has no factor 5; hence $5 \mid \overline{30a}$, i.e. $a \in \{0, 5\}$.

**By 3:** 3 is prime, so it must divide one of the factors. $\overline{30a}$ has digit sum $3 + a$ and $\overline{7b8}$ has digit sum $15 + b$, so we need $3 \mid a$ or $3 \mid b$.
- $a = 0$: always fine — any $b$: 10 pairs.
- $a = 5$: need $3 \mid b$, i.e. $b \in \{0, 3, 6, 9\}$: 4 pairs.

Total $10 + 4 = 14$.

**Answer: (D) 14**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0910-18.title: Rule out Maria at the top
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0910-18.body:
By the first fact, the best paid is Francis or Joana — never Maria.

Now if Joana were not the worst paid, the second fact would make Maria the best paid, which we just ruled out. So Joana is the worst paid. Then Joana is not the best paid, so Francis is.

Order: Francis (most), Maria, Joana (least).

**Answer: (B) Francis, Joana**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0910-26.title: Work backwards
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0910-26.body:
The two-digit multiples of 17 or 23 are $17, 34, 51, 68, 85$ and $23, 46, 69, 92$. Every digit appears at most once as a **second** digit among them, so going backwards each digit determines the one before it:
$$1 \leftarrow 5 \leftarrow 8 \leftarrow 6 \leftarrow 4 \leftarrow 3 \leftarrow 2 \leftarrow 9 \leftarrow 6 \leftarrow 4 \leftarrow \cdots$$
(from 51, 85, 68, 46, 34, 23, 92, 69, 46, …). So the sequence ends with $\ldots 6\,8\,5\,1$, and before the final $8\,5\,1$ the block $6, 4, 3, 2, 9$ repeats (read backwards).

Positions 2017, 2016, 2015 hold $1, 5, 8$. Position $2014 - k$ holds the $(k \bmod 5)$-th entry of $(6, 4, 3, 2, 9)$, counting from 0. Position 1 has $k = 2013$, and $2013 = 5\cdot402 + 3$, so it holds the entry with index 3, which is $2$.

**Answer: (A) 2**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0910-27.title: The difference is $9|a-b|$
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0910-27.body:
For the code $\overline{ab}$ the difference is $|(10a + b) - (10b + a)| = 9|a - b|$. Since $9 = 3^2$, this is a perfect square exactly when $|a - b|$ is a perfect square: $0, 1, 4$ or $9$.
- $|a - b| = 0$: 10 codes (00, 11, …, 99)
- $|a - b| = 1$: $9$ unordered pairs, 18 codes
- $|a - b| = 4$: pairs $(0,4), \ldots, (5,9)$: 6 pairs, 12 codes
- $|a - b| = 9$: 09 and 90: 2 codes

Total $10 + 18 + 12 + 2 = 42$.

**Answer: (E) 42**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0910-30.title: Midpoint of $BD$
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0910-30.body:
Let $L$ be the midpoint of $BD$.
- In triangle $ABD$, $ML$ joins the midpoints of $AD$ and $BD$, so $ML \parallel AB$ and $ML = \frac12 AB$.
- In triangle $DBC$, $LN$ joins the midpoints of $BD$ and $BC$, so $LN \parallel DC$ (i.e. parallel to $AC$) and $LN = \frac12 DC$.

Since $AB = DC$, we get $ML = LN$, so triangle $MLN$ is isosceles and $\angle LMN = \angle LNM$. Because $LN \parallel AC$, the alternate angles give $\angle LNM = \angle NMC = \alpha$. Hence $\angle LMC = \angle LMN + \angle NMC = 2\alpha$.

Finally $ML \parallel AB$, so $\angle LMC$ (between $ML$ and $MC$) equals $\angle BAC$ (between $AB$ and $AC$). Therefore $\angle BAC = 2\alpha$.

**Answer: (A) $2\alpha$**
